title: CDC: Req/Ack Handshake
constraints: Transfer 8-bit words from domain A to an unrelated domain B. A word is accepted on a rising `clk_a` edge where `a_valid && a_ready`. `a_valid` / `a_data` stay stable until accepted.
Every accepted word appears **exactly once**, in order, as a one-`clk_b`-cycle pulse on `b_valid` with `b_data`.

Control signals crossing domains must go through **2-flop synchronizers**: a word may not appear on `b_valid` sooner than 2 `clk_b` edges after capture, and must appear within 10. The data bus crosses unsynchronized, but it must be held stable while it is being sampled.
`a_ready` is 0 while a transfer is in flight. Each side has its own synchronous reset. Tested with A fast / B slow **and** A slow / B fast.
hints: Capture `a_data` into a holding register, then raise `req`. B synchronizes `req`, samples the (now stable) data, pulses `b_valid` and raises `ack`.
A synchronizes `ack` and drops `req`. B sees `req` low and drops `ack`. A sees `ack` low and becomes ready again: a 4-phase handshake.
Multi-bit buses must never go through individual synchronizers: the bits could be captured on different cycles. Synchronize one control bit and qualify the data with it.

examples.title: fast→slow
examples.input: clk_a 7 ns, clk_b 23 ns, a_valid always 1
examples.expected: every word arrives once, in order

examples.title: slow→fast
examples.expected: every word arrives once, in order
